chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Hariz ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
“None is kept perpetually in prison except three: one who is held for execution, a woman who apostatizes from Islam, and a thief after the cutting of the hand and the foot.”

key_terms.الْإِسْلَامِ: Islam, the religion from which apostasy is mentioned
key_terms.الْمَوْتِ: execution or death penalty in context
key_terms.قَطْعِ: amputation or cutting as a prescribed punishment

ai.seo_question: Who may be kept in perpetual imprisonment according to this hadith in Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning those for whom perpetual imprisonment applies. It identifies three categories in which continued confinement is prescribed, placing the report within the domain of judicial and penal rulings in Shia fiqh.
